ORDER Appellant-insurance company is aggrieved of award passed on 21.08.2012 in Claim Case No.34/2011 by Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pawai, district Panna (for short,
"Tribunal") under which company was directed to pay death compensation of Rs.3,63,000/- to respondents no.1 to 5-claimants under a joint and sever liability.

sentences.text: Cross-objections filed by respondents no. 6 and 7 are already dismissed for want of payment of statutory amount.

2. Appellant-insurance company is not challenging the facts of the accident but has contended that deceased Ramji Sharan was travelling on the mudguard of tractor and received fatal injuries when,
on account of rash and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:26509 2 MA-3401-2012 negligent driving by respondent no.6, deceased fell off the vehicle and sustained fatal injuries.

Thus,
according to appellant-insurance company, the risk of deceased, who was an unauthorized traveler on the mudguard of tractor, was not covered under the insurance policy.
It, therefore, seeks complete exoneration from the liability.

sentences.text: 3. Appeal has been opposed by respondents no.1 to 5 and also by respondent no.7, the owner of the vehicle, who has filed written arguments, in the light of order dated 11.03.2026.

4. Reading of claim petition itself discloses that victim was sitting on the tractor and on account of jolt felt, resulting from rash and negligent driving by respondent no.6, deceased fell off the tractor and sustained fatal injuries.

This admitted position, that deceased was travelling on the mudguard of the tractor, is manifested even in the statements of claimants Lavkush (AW-1) and Dharmendra (AW-3) and also of witness Ramasre (AW-2).

Although driver Ram Milan Kushwah (NAW-1)
challenged all these facts, but no cross-appeal was filed by him, and even cross-objections filed in the case have already been dismissed.

5. Ex. D-2 is the insurance policy of offending tractor which has given insurance cover to only one employee in addition to the basic OD cover and the TP cover and that too if the vehicle is used for agricultural and forestry purposes.
Here, the act of giving lift to a person can not be taken on its face value, having an agricultural or forestry purpose.

Thus, there was apparent breach of the term of the insurance policy and the same fact was stated by Rameshwar Prasad Ahirwar (NAW-2) examined on behalf of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:26509 3 MA-3401-2012 appellant-insurance company, which was not challenged in cross- examination either.

Para 12 of the impugned award reveals that the use of vehicle against the purpose mentioned in insurance policy was not at all considered and Tribunal evaded this prominent ground of defence while deciding the liability issue.
6. Respondent no.7, the owner, has supported the finding given by the Tribunal.

Citing some case laws it has held that in cases where negligence on the part of deceased was not proved and breach of the policy terms was also not proved, the insurer is liable to satisfy the award irrespective of the fact that deceased was travelling on the mudguard of tractor.

These citations have not been placed before this Court either by respondents no.1 to 5 or respondent no.7, but citations available on internet with same nomenclature suggest that these two cases were decided on 31.08.2010 and 26.06.2008 respectively and in both of them, placing reliance on various decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court

, the Single Bench of this High Court held that the finding recorded by the Tribunal, that appellant-insurance company was liable to indemnify the insured under these circumstances, is contrary to law and, accordingly, the appeal filed by appellant-insurance company in both these cases was allowed.
Thus, verdicts given in the case laws cited by Tribunal were supporting the contention of appellant-insurance company.
If the respondents were relying upon some other decision, it was their duty to place it before this Court.

As they submitted none , this Court cannot accept their contention that despite there being no risk covered under the insurance policy of a p e r s o n t r a v e l l i n g o n t h e m u d g u a r d o f t r a c t o r , t h e N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2026:MPHC-JBP:26509 4 MA-3401-2012 appellant-insurance company was still liable to pay compensation for his death in an accident.

7. In terms of aforesaid discussion, this appeal is allowed and appellant-insurance company is completely exonerated from the liability to pay any compensation under the impugned award for the death of Ramji Sharan, who was travelling on the mudguard of a tractor when he sustained fatal injuries.
He was not an innocent third party vis-a-vis the offending tractor.
